comparisons.peer_topic: Litigation and Regulatory Charges in Restructuring
comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring charges included $780 million for R2 litigation in 2024, a $1.2 billion benefit from VLSI litigation developments in 2023, a $401 million EC fine and $353 million Tower acquisition termination fee in 2023, and a $1.2 billion benefit in 2022 from an annulled EC fine.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose termination fees related to M&A regulatory hurdles, though Intel's fee was paid for a failed prior acquisition (Tower) while AMD's is a contingent future liability for a pending deal (ZT Systems). Intel explicitly references a $353 million termination fee incurred in 2023 due to the inability to timely obtain regulatory approvals for the Tower acquisition, whereas AMD discloses a $300 million termination fee payable if its ZT Systems acquisition does not close by August 17, 2025, subject to regulatory approvals.

sentences.text: The Agreement provides that if the Acquisition is not completed by August 17, 2025, subject to two automatic extensions until February 17, 2026, the Company will pay a termination fee of $300 million.
The Acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2025, subject to certain regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

2023 charges also included a $401 million charge for an EC-imposed fine and a $353 million termination fee in connection with our inability to timely obtain required regulatory approvals needed to acquire Tower.
